title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 140-3, 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): Grothendieck fixes a group 𝔊 (profinite or adelic, e.g. points of a group scheme over ℤ such as SL2/PGL2). It contains an orientation-preserving part 𝔊^+, an orientation character ε_𝔊 : 𝔊 → {±1}, and a subgroup 𝔊^φ. Its elements ρ, σ, τ are images (under a map π from a cartographic/triangle-type group) of the standard generators. Here τ is an orientation-reversing involution acting by τ(σ)=σ^{-1} and τ(ρ)=σ^{-1}ρ^{-1}σ. The previous page set 𝔊^φ_τ = {1,τ}·𝔊^φ. ε_0 is a distinguished (central) element. The goal is to define a group Z_{ρ,σ} and a map γ_{ρ,σ}, a 'GT-like' symmetry group of the pair (ρ,σ) inside 𝔊.

Definition: Z_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(𝔊^+) × Ẑ^* × μ × μ, with μ={±1}, is the set of quadruples (u, μ, ε2, ε3) such that:
(a) u(ρ) = α ρ α^{-1} for some α ∈ 𝔊^φ_τ with ε_𝔊(α)=ε3;
(b) u(σ) = β σ β^{-1} for some β ∈ 𝔊^φ_τ with ε_𝔊(β)=ε2;
(c) u(ε_0) = ε_0^μ, a cyclotomic-type exponent μ ∈ Ẑ^*;
(d) u normalises 𝔊^φ and induces the identity on the quotient (𝔊^+/𝔊^φ)/Im π.
A left-margin note seems to record a consequence of the conditions: compatibility with τ forces ε2ε3=1, i.e. ε=ε2=ε3 ∈ {±1}.

Proposition: Z_{ρ,σ} is a subgroup of the product group.

Proof as begun on this page:
- (c) and (d) each clearly define subgroups.
- Since τ(σ)=σ^{-1}, condition (b) is equivalent to (b'): u(σ) is 𝔊^φ-conjugate to σ^{ε2}. In this form, together with (d) (u preserves 𝔊^φ), closure under composition is clear: the signs multiply.
- Grothendieck remarks he does not think (a) alone defines a subgroup. The reason is that writing α=α0τ gives conjugation by α0σ, and σ need not lie in 𝔊^φ.
- So he proves instead that the set 𝒢_{(a,b)} is a subgroup of 𝒢_{(b)}.
- The next page does the computation. If ε3=1, take α''=u'(α)α'. If ε3=−1, write α=α0τ and use ρ^{-1}=στ(ρ) and the fact that u'(σ) is a 𝔊^φ-conjugate of σ^{±1} (from (b)) to produce α'' ∈ 𝔊^φ_τ up to a central sign.

Purpose: this is a finite/adelic 'shadow' of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type condition. Automorphisms send the generator classes to conjugates of themselves (twisted by orientation), together with a cyclotomic exponent. It presumably serves to define a homomorphism γ_{ρ,σ} from the GT/Galois-type group, or from Z_{ρ,σ}, to an outer-automorphism group of the target.
errors: No genuine mathematical error on this page. The claim that (b) is equivalent to (b') needs τ(σ)=σ^{-1}. It also tacitly needs (d) (u preserves 𝔊^φ) to get closure; Grothendieck uses this implicitly.

Small gap: closure under inverses is not addressed. It is automatic only if Z is finite/compact or the conditions are symmetric; for profinite 𝔊 it follows by a compactness/closure argument that he does not state.

Small gap: in case ε3=−1 the element α'' produced on the next page is only determined up to a central sign ±1 and lies a priori in 𝔊, not necessarily in 𝔊^φ_τ. Grothendieck himself flags this ('si possible'), so membership in 𝔊^φ_τ is not yet proved here.

ideas.what: Group of automorphisms of a target group 𝔊^+ sending images of the cartographic generators ρ, σ to conjugates of themselves (possibly by orientation-reversing elements), together with a cyclotomic exponent μ ∈ Ẑ^* acting on a central element.
ideas.modern_name: GT-type stabiliser / 'GT-shadows' on finite or adelic quotients; normaliser of the braided/cartographic data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; recent 'GT-shadows' by Dolgushev and collaborators (2021–)
ideas.where_published: The general programme (Galois/GT action on cartographic groups) is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche; this specific construction is not published to my knowledge.

ideas.what: Reformulating a 'conjugate by an element of the extended group 𝔊^φ_τ with prescribed orientation sign' condition as 'conjugate in 𝔊^φ to σ^{±1}', using that τ inverts σ, to show closure.
ideas.modern_name: elementary group theory (twisted conjugacy classes, orientation character)

ideas.what: Observation that the ρ-condition alone is not a subgroup condition, but is one relative to the σ-condition, since σ intervenes in the orientation-reversing case through τ(ρ)=σ^{-1}ρ^{-1}σ.
ideas.modern_name: interdependence of the GT generator conditions (analogous to how hexagon and 2-cycle relations interact)

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines, for a homomorphism of the (extended, orientation-including) cartographic group into a finite or adelic group 𝔊 (e.g. points of a group scheme over ℤ), a group Z_{ρ,σ} of automorphisms preserving the generator conjugacy classes twisted by a cyclotomic exponent and orientation signs. This is essentially the 'GT-shadow'/finite-quotient approach to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group developed only recently (Dolgushev et al.). His variant includes the orientation-reversing involution τ and adelic/algebraic-group targets, which the modern literature does not seem to treat.
missed.quote: Z_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(G^+) × Ẑ^* × μ × μ ... a) ∃ α ∈ G^φ_τ, avec ε_G(α)=ε3, u(ρ)=α(ρ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could suggest extending GT-shadow techniques to the cartographic group with reflections and to targets like SL2(Ẑ) or adelic groups, relating GT/Galois actions to representation varieties of triangle groups.

missed.claim: The construction is announced as leading to a map γ_{ρ,σ}, and the case of 𝔊 = adelic integral points of a group scheme over ℤ is deferred ('J'y reviendrai'). Whether these were completed in the archive is unclear.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A scheme-theoretic version would give algebraic-group-valued invariants of the GT action, which is not standard in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical, mostly routine subgroup verification. The page itself proves nothing deep, but it documents Grothendieck working out GT-like symmetry groups attached to representations of cartographic groups into finite or adelic groups, including orientation reversal. That approach resembles the recent 'GT-shadows' programme, which is moderately interesting historically.
transcription_corrections: 'τ(σ) = −ε' should almost certainly read 'τ(σ) = σ^{-1}' (τ inverts σ). The next page uses τ(ρ)=σ^{-1}(ρ^{-1}), i.e. conjugation.
'la condition c') définit un sous-groupe' should be 'la condition b')' (referring to the reformulation (5 bis) b').
'G_{(b)}', 'G_{(a,b)}' are script 𝒢_{(b)}, 𝒢_{(a,b)} (subsets of the product group), not the group G.
Groups written G, G^φ, G^+ are fraktur 𝔊, 𝔊^φ, 𝔊^+ (consistent with the previous page). ε_G is ε_𝔊, the orientation character.
'ce qui prouvera la [?]' is likely 'ce qui prouvera la proposition'.
In condition d) the quotient is likely (𝔊^+/𝔊^φ)/Im π, rather than (G^φ/G^φ).
